upserts.markdown: Red is the color of intensity — it pulls the eye faster than any other hue. It signals both danger and desire, showing up in stop signs and warning labels as readily as in roses and valentines. Across many cultures it carries luck and celebration, from wedding garments to festival lanterns. Physically, it sits at the long-wavelength end of the visible spectrum, the last color we see before light fades into infrared. Warm and insistent, red rarely goes unnoticed.
